data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the same 5 files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, pince.desktop, pince.sh, .gitignore) and found no malicious content. The only disagreement was caused by a technical error (HTTP 400) in the first model's audit of .gitignore, not substantive disagreement. The second model successfully audited .gitignore and confirmed it's a standard gitignore file. All files contain standard AUR packaging practices: VCS sources with SKIP checksums (normal for git), standard desktop entry, and a legitimate privilege escalation wrapper using pkexec. No injection patterns, no execution of fetched content, no suspicious network operations.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a technical error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen model's audit of .gitignore, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited the same file and found it safe. This is not a substantive disagreement about security - both models agreed on all other files.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .gitignore due to API error (HTTP 400)
learnings: Technical errors (API failures, timeouts) should not result in 'inconclusive' package verdicts when the error affects only a single low-risk file like .gitignore
When multiple models review the same package and one has a technical error on a specific file, the other model's successful audit of that file should resolve the disagreement
Files like .gitignore, .SRCINFO, and .desktop are low-risk and their audit failures should not block a package verdict when other models have successfully reviewed them
